subject: Follow-up: hosting preference and migration constraints — NovaHealth
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sandoval <alex.sandoval@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + clarifying questions on hosting preference and migration path

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time this morning. High-level recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a tailored follow-up.

Call summary (quick):
- Primary need: low-latency inference for clinical summarization (60–120 ms target p95 on common requests) and strict PHI handling.
- Current stack: customer-facing API on a legacy on-prem GPU cluster + some traffic via OpenAPI vendor for burst.
- Procurement timeline: evaluating options this quarter; procurement lead looped in.

Questions for qualification (please reply inline):
1) Data residency / PHI: you mentioned HIPAA requirements — do you need fully on-premise deployment, or is a Private VPC with customer-managed KMS acceptable?
2) Traffic profile: is the 80/20 split between short clinical prompts and long-document summarization still accurate? Typical prompt lengths you see?
3) Migration appetite: would you consider a phased approach (1) burst + hosted API for surface traffic, (2) Dedicated reserved capacity for baseline, (3) Private/VPC for full cutover)? Or must the long-term plan be full private at cutover?

Attached: rough risk matrix we discussed and a short hosting options brief (redwood-hosting-options-v2.pdf).

Next steps we suggest:
- Karthik to confirm Dedicated capacity sizing and latency SLAs.
- Marissa to run a quick perf delta estimate for quantized LLM variants vs your current model.
- Alex/Procurement to share target decision date and any contract constraints.

Available windows for a 30–45m technical follow-up this week: Thu 11:00–13:00 PT or Fri 09:00–11:00 PT.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129
From: Alex Sandoval <alex.sandoval@novahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying questions on hosting preference and migration path

Soojin — thanks for the recap, helpful. Quick answers inline:  

1) Data residency / PHI: We cannot send PHI to shared multi-tenant endpoints without a BAA and proof of encrypted key separation. A Private VPC with customer KMS is acceptable and preferred; fully on-prem is an option for later if latency/regulatory checks require it.

2) Traffic profile: Yes — ~80% short prompts (50–120 tokens) for chart summarization and triage; ~20% long docs (1k–5k tokens) for discharge notes. P95 latency targets: 120ms for short prompts, up to 1.5s acceptable for long-docs.

3) Migration appetite: We prefer a phased route. Immediate check: can Redwood support a hybrid pattern where we run baseline traffic on Dedicated reserved capacity but route the heaviest long-doc workflows to a Private deployment until we validate correctness? Also need KV cache behavior across routes (we'd prefer cache locality to preserve prompt context).

Procurement note: we are targeting an internal EoQ decision (by 2026-09-24). Procurement is looking for a draft SOW + indicative pricing to start the vendor review.

I can do Thu 11:00 PT.

Alex
Director of Engineering — ML Platforms
NovaHealth
alex.sandoval@novahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-3210

--
On Tue, Aug 27, 2026 at 09:15 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time this morning. High-level recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a tailored follow-up.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sandoval <alex.sandoval@novahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick recap + clarifying questions on hosting preference and migration path

Alex / team — great conversation. A few technical clarifications and items we'll include in the draft SOW.

Notes / clarifying questions:  
- Hybrid routing: yes, we can support routing by traffic class. Typical approach: Dedicated reserved pool for baseline short prompt traffic (keeps cold-starts and token cost predictable), and a Private VPC for the long-document pipelines that require strict PHI controls. We'll document latency tradeoffs and KV cache locality (cache will be local to the runtime; cross-route cache-sharing is not automatic).

- KV cache & session affinity: If you need cache hits across Dedicated <-> Private we can implement a prefix-based routing with fallback, but this requires deterministic prefix hashing and will add complexity. Otherwise we recommend keeping session affinity per deployment to guarantee p95 SLAs.

- Model variants & quantization: we'll produce an estimate for float16 vs 4-bit quantized candidate and the expected delta in per-token cost and latency. For long-doc summarization we often recommend an FP16 variant to preserve quality.

- Cutover approach: we typically recommend a three-step migration: 1) low-risk surface traffic to Hosted (if you want burst capacity quickly), 2) baseline on Dedicated with SMAs and monitoring, 3) full Private/VPC cutover for PHI-only workloads. Since you asked for phased, our SOW will include milestone gates and rollback criteria.

Attachments: I attached a starter mutual action plan and a lightweight risk matrix (nova_risk_matrix.xlsx and mutual-action-plan.docx).

Questions for you (quick):
- Can procurement share any contract minimum term constraints?
- Any data exfiltration scanning or restrictive egress rules for the Private environment we should plan for?

I'll prepare an indicative sizing + cost back-of-envelope for Dedicated (GPU type, baseline throughput) and a sketch for Private sizing. Will aim to send by EOD Wed.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0781
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-28T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying questions on hosting preference and migration path

Alex — looping in Procurement cadence and next steps. We're drafting a short SOW + indicative pricing and will include two lanes: (A) Dedicated-first baseline with Private VPC for PHI cutover, (B) Private-first (on-prem option) with optional burst to Hosted for overflow.

Quick bullets on timelines and asks from NovaHealth to accelerate:  
- Confirmation of target decision date: you flagged 2026-09-24 — confirm so we can prioritize the procurement package.
- Expected monthly baseline QPS and peak burst QPS (so we size reserved GPUs vs burst pools).
- Any security questionnaire we should expect (if you can pre-share vendor security checklist or the egress/scanning constraints it speeds reviews).
- Contract preferences on term length and auto-renewal (procurement indicated preferences in call).

We will:  
- Share SOW + indicative pricing + architecture sketch by 2026-08-31 EOD.
- Include a checklist for the on-prem/private handoff, required network info (VPC peering, transit, KMS key IDs), and a proposed canary plan for the first 2 weeks of cutover.

DocuSign and contract intake: we'll provide a preliminary quote that procurement can use for internal vendor review; once aligned we'll send a DocuSign link.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (206) 555-4490
